questions.q: What is the exact purpose of the `<!DOCTYPE html>` declaration in an HTML5 document?
questions.a: The `<!DOCTYPE html>` declaration tells the browser to render the page in standards mode (HTML5) rather than quirks mode. A wrong answer (e.g., "it defines the root element" or "it links the CSS file") reveals the student confuses the doctype with the `<html>` tag or `<link>` tag, indicating they haven't grasped that the doctype is a mode switch, not an element.

questions.q:
A student writes `My Page

Welcome

`. Explain why the `

` will not appear as a heading on the rendered page.
questions.a: The `<head>` section only contains metadata — content inside it is never rendered visually. The `<h1>` belongs in `<body>`. If the student says "the heading will appear but without styling" or "browsers automatically move it to body", they hold the misconception that `<head>` is a visible header area (like `<header>`), confusing semantic structure with layout.

questions.q: Write the minimal HTML5 code to set the character encoding to UTF-8, make the page responsive on mobile devices, and set the browser tab title to "Project Demo".
questions.a:
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Project Demo</title>
</head>
<body></body>
</html>
```
A wrong answer missing `charset` or `viewport` or placing `<title>` outside `<head>` shows the student cannot apply the three essential metadata tags together, often because they memorize tags in isolation rather than as a required set for modern web pages.

questions.q: Compare the roles of `<meta name="description">` and `<meta name="viewport">`. Why would omitting each hurt a real-world website differently?
questions.a: `<meta name="description">` provides a snippet for search engine results (SEO); omitting it lets search engines auto-generate a less relevant summary, reducing click-through rates. `<meta name="viewport">` controls mobile layout scaling; omitting it causes desktop-like rendering on phones, forcing horizontal scrolling and hurting usability. A student who says both affect "appearance" or "SEO" fails to distinguish between search-engine metadata and browser-rendering instructions.

questions.q: A webpage loads a CSS file via `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">` placed at the bottom of `<body>` instead of in `<head>`. Evaluate the impact on page load performance and visual stability.
questions.a: Placing the stylesheet link in `<body>` delays CSS parsing until the browser reaches that point, causing a flash of unstyled content (FOUC) and increasing perceived load time. Best practice is to put `<link rel="stylesheet">` in `<head>` so styles are fetched and parsed early. A student who claims "it doesn't matter because the browser loads everything anyway" ignores the critical rendering path and the browser's sequential parsing behavior.

questions.q: Design a new metadata tag (not in HTML5 standard) that could help a browser automatically detect the primary language of a page's visible text content. Write its syntax and explain how it would differ from the existing `lang` attribute on `<html>`.
questions.a: Proposed tag: `<meta name="primary-language" content="hi">` placed in `<head>`. Unlike `lang="hi"` on `<html>` (which declares the document's default language for inheritance), this meta tag would explicitly signal the dominant language of the *rendered text* for translation tools or screen readers, even if the document contains mixed languages. A poor answer merely replicates `lang` or suggests a `<script>` solution, showing inability to innovate within metadata constraints.
